Acknowledgements
This training manual is the result of the collaboration of the WHO Global Health Ethics Unit (GHE) in the 
Department of Knowledge, Ethics and Research (KER), the Department of Emergency Risk Management 
and Humanitarian Response (ERM) and the Department of Pandemic and Epidemic Diseases (PED). The 
development of this manual was led by Andreas Reis (GHE) with assistance from Abha Saxena, Coordinator

blocks.title: Introduction
blocks.content:
Epidemics, emergencies and disasters raise many ethical issues for the people involved, who include 
responders, public health specialists and policy‑makers. This training manual provides material on ethical 
issues in research, surveillance and patient care in these difficult contexts, as well as related issues to reduce 
risks before, during and after events.
The idea for this manual can be traced back to a  WHO technical consultation on Research ethics in 
international epidemic response (World Health Organization, 2010). In the resulting report, the experts took 
positions on three main is

Core competence 5: Ability to explain how publication ethics are 
related to public health surveillance or research in emergencies

to share and publicize the relevant findings in due time. Such scientific knowledge can be obtained during 
routine surveillance. Therefore, data collection might have been initiated without proper ethics oversight.
